newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PARIS ST GERMAIN LOSE MORE GROUND ON MONACO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARIS ST GERMAIN LOSE MORE GROUND ON MONACO.

text.p: Paris St Germain lost more ground in their French league title chase with a 1-1 draw at home to Rennes on Saturday.
Monaco beat Lille 2-0 on Friday and are now 12 points ahead of second-placed PSG with just six matches left.
The Parisians, in shock after the news that goalkeeper Bernard Lama had failed a dope test for cannabis, stayed firmly in second spot as their main rivals were unable to win.
Strasbourg lost in Nancy 2-0 while Nantes, now unbeaten in their last 25 matches, drew with Marseille 1-1. Nantes and Strasbourg are on 53 points, two points behind Paris St Germain.
PSG had to come from behind after Rennes had opened the scoring through a 37th minute Stephane Guivarch penalty. Substitute Cyrille Pouget equalised 18 minutes from time.
"It's too late for the title but I still firmly believe we'll stick to our second place," said PSG president Bernard Brochant.
"But if we want to keep this second place, we must stop drawing at home," he added.
Goalscorer Pouget said: "I'm happy I scored but a draw at home is not a real morale booster before our clash against Liverpool next Thursday."
Liverpool visit the French capital for a European Cupwinners Cup semi-final first leg.
Nantes were close to catching PSG as they led Marseille until the very end thanks to a 22nd minute Japhet N'Doram goal.
But Marc Libbra equalised in injury time, giving the former European champions a point which should save them from relegation.
The game ended in confusion and Marseille's Bulgarian midfielder Iordan Lechkov was sent off.
The Canaries have not lost in their last 25 league matches but they will have to wait for next season to equal their league record of 32 unbeaten games.
Montpellier and Bordeaux battled it out for the fourth time this season, Montpellier taking the points with a 2-0 win.
Bordeaux, who were without former European footballer of the year Jean-Pierre Papin, had already lost 2-1 to Montpellier in a French Cup quarter-final last week.
Montpellier's Ibrahim Bakayoko got both goals, in the 5th and 13th minutes.
Bordeaux had the better of the early meetings, winning the first two clashes -- a league tie at home and a League Cup semi-final in February.
They will hope to book their place in next season's UEFA Cup when they play Strasbourg in the League Cup final next Saturday.
